changelog.text:
## [0.6.0] - 2026-11-02

### Changed

- The "Turn off all plugins" switch in Settings → Plugins now sits in a card like the other settings.
- Mumcord starts faster: the code that has to load before the first screen is about a third smaller (Settings, the setup wizard, watch together, screen share, the server browser, the extra windows and code highlighting in chat now load only when they are first opened), and release builds no longer contain the built-in test data (#323)
- Mumcord now opens with a **start screen** (the logo on the theme background with a slim loading bar) instead of an empty white window and a bare "Loading…" text. The window only appears once the start screen is drawn, the start screen follows your system theme (or the fixed theme you picked) and fades into the app when it is ready; with reduced motion it switches without movement (#323)

### Added

- Plugin authors get the SDK and tools from crates.io: `cargo install mumcord-plugin` installs the command-line tool, and `mumcord-plugin new` creates projects that depend on the `mumcord-plugin-sdk` release instead of a git checkout
- A plugin installed from a server's suggestion is remembered at once, so the suggestion does not come back if you remove the plugin again.
- **Plugins**: small add-ons that give Mumcord new features. A new **Settings > Plugins** page has five tabs: **Installed** (switch a plugin on or off, change its permissions, settings and who it talks to, see diagnostics, export or reset its data, remove it with or without its data), **Browse** (official plugins by category, with search), **Updates**, **Repositories** and, with Developer mode on, **Developer**. No plugin is installed by default. Plugins also run while you are not connected to a server. **Plugins** is in the command palette too.
- Installing or updating a plugin now shows a progress bar with the downloaded size, then "Checking signature", "Unpacking" and "Starting"; a failed download can be retried from the install dialog.
- Installing a plugin first shows an **install prompt** in plain language: what it wants to do, each permission marked green, yellow or red, required ones fixed and optional ones as switches. Permissions can be changed later and take effect at once. Plugins can never read your chat text, files, microphone, certificates or passwords.
- A plugin can ask to **recognise certain chat messages**, for example a game fit pasted into chat, so it can show them as a card. The install prompt says in the plugin's own words what it recognises; it then gets only matching messages in your current channel (at most 4 KB each, never from people you blocked) and no other chat text.
- A plugin card now **takes the place of the chat message it belongs to** (for example a pasted fit or a poll) instead of appearing below it, and counted `!poll` votes can be tucked away. Each replaced or hidden message shows the plugin's icon and name, and **Show original text** brings the message back. Older messages in a channel get their cards too, without votes being counted again.
- Plugins show up where you use Mumcord: a **Plugins strip** under the channel list (one icon per plugin, a small panel for the active one and an expand button; it can be collapsed), cards in the chat, **slash commands** such as `/roll`, a small badge next to names (one at a time; choose which in Settings), a section in profile cards, entries in a person's right-click menu, and plugin windows. Messages sent by a plugin are marked "via" the plugin, and a plugin's own plain-text fallback line is hidden for people who see its card.
- Plugin chat features (cards, recognised messages, `!` commands, replies) now work in the chat of **every server you are connected to**, not only the one you talk on; a plugin's reply or card always appears in the chat it belongs to.
- Plugins can send you **notifications**; they appear in the notification centre under a new **Plugins** category, can be switched off per plugin and stay silent in Do Not Disturb.
- Plugins can exchange data with the same plugin on other people's Mumcord in your channel (for example a shared poll). It travels over the normal voice server, so standard Mumble servers need nothing, other clients ignore it, and you choose who may see it.
- A poll created right after someone in your channel installs Poll now reaches them without rejoining: a newly installed plugin is announced to others at once, and plugins learn when someone starts running them.
- **Plugin updates** have their own setting: install automatically (default), notify only, or off. An update that asks for more permissions or comes from a different author always waits for your approval, a plugin that fails to start after an update is rolled back, and a plugin can be pinned to its current version.
- When a plugin update brings **new optional permissions** (for example `!poll` voting for people without Mumcord), they stay off but are offered in **Settings > Plugins > Updates**, with suggested ones already selected; the plugin shows "New permissions" in Installed until you save or choose Not now. A plugin can also open its own permission settings after you click it, such as a "Turn on !poll voting" hint.
- **Servers can suggest plugins**: a server's Mumbot can recommend plugins, which appear in the notification centre with Install, Details, Not now and Don't ask again for this server. Nothing is installed without your approval.
- **Third-party repositories**: add up to 10 repositories of your own in Settings > Plugins > Repositories (shown with the repository name and key fingerprint first). Their plugins are labelled "Unofficial" everywhere, the first install from each repository shows a warning, and a repository whose signing key changes is paused until you confirm.
- **Developer mode** (Settings > Advanced) adds a Developer tab to load, reload and unload a plugin from a folder, with its log. Such plugins are marked "Developer plugin" and are unloaded when Developer mode is turned off. A plugin SDK, the `mumcord-plugin` command-line tool for authors and a project template are available (Apache-2.0).
- Plugin layouts can now have a row where one entry fills the width next to a fixed button (for example a saved fit next to **Copy fitting**), and plugin buttons can show a small second line such as who saved an entry and when.
- The **Plugins** entry in the Settings sidebar shows how many plugin updates (and new optional permissions) are waiting.
- An installed plugin's permissions list what its chat patterns recognise under "Recognise certain chat messages", as the install prompt does.
- `mumcord://plugins/<id>` links open the details of an official plugin in Browse; they never install anything by themselves.
- Four official plugins, each available in all 24 Mumcord languages:
  - **Poll**: ask a question with 2 to 10 options, see live results in the chat card and the panel, and end the poll when done. Votes are counted once per person.
  - **Dice roller**: `/roll` with notation like `d20`, `2d6+3`, advantage and disadvantage, and drop lowest or highest, plus quick-roll buttons and a built-in help. Rolls are made together with others in the channel so nobody can cheat, and each result says Verified, Unverified (rolled alone) or Not revealed.
  - **Echolings**: a small pet that lives in your Plugins strip, with 5 species, 4 growth stages and 3 colours. Pat, feed, play with it or let it nap; it never dies, sleeps when you are on Do Not Disturb and has no paid items or sounds. Friends see your pet as a badge and in your profile card, can react to it and visit it, and there are two mini-games, Echo Echo and Snack Race.
  - **Mumbot Music**: control a Mumbot music bot from Mumcord (now playing, skip, stop, volume, queue, add tracks). Right-click the bot and choose **Configure bot**, enter its address and API key and test the connection. The key is kept in your system keychain.
- Mumbot now introduces itself to Mumcord, so Mumcord knows which users are bots and what they can do; "Configure bot" appears only on bots that offer music.
- Safety: plugins run in a sealed sandbox with no access to your network, files or audio other than what Mumcord offers them, and with limits on memory and time. A plugin that keeps crashing is turned off, and nothing affects your voice. **Turn off all plugins** (Settings > Plugins and the command palette) stops them all at once, and starting Mumcord with `--no-plugins` loads none. Official plugins are signed and checked on install and after every Mumcord update; a **kill switch** can disable a plugin that turns out to be harmful, with the reason shown, and is checked once a day even when plugin updates are off.
- Privacy: checking for plugins sends no identifiers and no list of what you have installed. Plugin data stays on your computer, removing a plugin keeps its data for 30 days unless you delete it, and see PRIVACY.md for the details.
- A second sound theme, **Rich**: new, fuller notification sounds for connecting to voice, new messages, mentions, microphone mute and unmute, deafen and undeafen, someone joining or leaving your channel, leaving voice, being kicked and being banned. Settings > Sounds has a **Sound theme** switch with a preview button to choose between Rich (the default) and **Classic**, the familiar short synthesized tones; the theme applies to every notification sound at once (#325)
- Quitting Mumcord while you are in a voice channel plays a short, distinctive goodbye sound, so you notice that you just left voice. It plays on every real quit (window close set to Quit, tray Quit, the quit menu or shortcut, and restarting for an update), never when Mumcord only minimises to the tray or when you are not in voice, and it follows the output volume, deafen, the sound theme and its own switch in Settings > Sounds (on by default). Mumcord waits for it at most 1.5 seconds, in parallel with closing the connections; a second quit request exits at once. The sound is local only: others still see the normal leave from the server (#325)
- Switching to another channel while you are in voice plays its own short channel-switch sound instead of the connect sound, with its own switch in Settings > Sounds (on by default) and a variant in both sound themes (#325)

### Fixed

- A plugin is no longer stopped while your system keychain asks you to unlock it or to allow access (KWallet, GNOME Keyring, macOS Keychain), and saving a plugin password while that prompt is open no longer holds up other plugins. If the prompt is not answered within 2 minutes, the plugin is told secrets are unavailable.
- Plugins: old compiled copies of plugins no longer pile up on disk; Mumcord removes the ones that are no longer needed each time it starts
- Closing a full profile card with Escape right after using a button in it (for example a plugin button that then greys out) no longer stops that profile card from opening again.
- Plugins that keep data per identity (such as Echolings) no longer fail to start with "invalid" when no server is open yet, for example right after installing them or after restarting Mumcord; they use your default identity until you open a server
- Keyboard: when a dialog changes its content (for example a plugin dialog switching from its setup form to its player), the focus now stays in the dialog, so Escape and Tab keep working.
- A plugin card that answers no chat message, such as the Dice result after `/roll`, now shows at the bottom of the chat at its own time instead of above the first date divider
- The example test scenario of `mumcord-plugin` (`scenarios/hello.yaml`) passes again for a plugin created with `mumcord-plugin new`
- A plugin card now replaces its chat line right away, even when the line arrives after the card (for example a Poll card and its "Vote with !poll" line), on other clients and in your own chat
- The chat stays scrolled to the newest message when a plugin card appears or grows after its message (for example while its images load); if you scrolled up to read, it stays where you are
- A plugin dialog that shows a web page (for example the EVE fit plugin's fitting wheel) is now large (up to 960 × 720 pixels, shrinking with the window) instead of the narrow dialog size, and the page can show its own icons and images
- A plugin card for your own fresh message (for example the dice card after /roll) now shows at the bottom next to that message instead of above the older messages
- Screen readers now read a chat line a plugin replaced as its card (e.g. "Card from Poll: Lunch at noon?") and no longer read lines a plugin hid.
- A plugin that uses the system keychain (such as Mumbot Music) is no longer stopped as "took too long" when the keychain answers slowly.
- Text you are typing into a plugin's field (for example a track URL in Mumbot Music) no longer disappears when another part of the plugin's window changes, such as a new song starting, and a field or slider the plugin resets (for example the track field after **Add track**) no longer shows your old entry again.
- Plugin cards in the chat no longer get their own scrollbar: a taller card is cut off with a soft fade and **Show more** expands it.
- Pasting with Ctrl+V works again on some Linux desktops
- A plugin that could not be loaded now keeps its name (in your language) and icon in **Settings > Plugins > Installed** instead of showing its internal id
- A plugin window that shows a web page (for example the EVE fit fitting wheel) now opens right after installing or updating the plugin, instead of only after restarting Mumcord
- A plugin button that leads to its permissions (for example Poll's **Turn on !poll voting**) now opens that plugin's permissions in **Settings > Plugins > Installed** instead of only the list
- The Poll chat card shows its top three options in full again instead of fading the third one behind **Show more**
- The "Change" link in the Settings sidebar's "Active preset" card no longer sticks out of the card when the preset name is long (#321)
- The "simultaneously connected servers" number field in Settings > Server is no longer stretched across the whole card; it is now as narrow as the number it holds (#320)
- Plugins shared with **Friends** only now reach someone you add as a friend while they are already in your channel, instead of only after one of you rejoins

### Internal

- Plugin runtime (Epic 3.1, #268): the new `crates/plugins` runs plugins as WebAssembly components in wasmtime without WASI, so a plugin can only call what Mumcord offers (for now only its own log). Each plugin gets its own store with a 32 MiB memory limit and a CPU deadline per call (500 ms for start, 50 ms otherwise); a plugin that loops, runs out of memory or crashes is stopped while everything else keeps running, restarts with back-off and stays off after 3 failures in 10 minutes. The first version of the plugin API (`mumcord:plugin@1.0.0`) lives in `crates/plugins/wit/`. Not linked into the app yet.
- Plugin system groundwork (Epic 3.1): empty `crates/plugin-sdk` (plugin SDK) and `tools/mumcord-plugin` (author CLI) crates, both Apache-2.0, and every new dependency of the epic added up front: `minisign-verify` and `minisign` for repository signatures, `hmac` for peer keys, `toml` for repository sources, `wit-bindgen` for the SDK and `serde-saphyr` for CLI test scenarios. `crates/plugins` now depends on the store. Not visible in the app yet.
- Plugin manifest and package format (Epic 3.1, #269): `manifest.json` is parsed strictly as untrusted input (size and length caps, known permissions and categories only, safe relative paths, caret ranges on the plugin API), with a published JSON schema in `crates/plugins/schema/`. `.mcplugin` zips are checked before anything touches the disk (at most 5 MiB, 200 files and 8 MiB unpacked, no symlinks, encryption or `..` paths, image-only assets), verified against the sha256 and size from the index, and installed atomically. Translated plugin names follow the app language with English fallback; sideloaded packages cannot take an official or reserved id. Not visible in the app yet.
